title: Spanish Civil War (1936–1939)
key_facts: Conflict between Republican government and Nationalist rebels led by Francisco Franco
Major ideological testing ground for WWII tactics and weapons
International involvement: Germany/Italy supported Nationalists, USSR/International Brigades supported Republicans
Approximately 500,000 deaths; massive displacement and cultural destruction
causes: Political polarization between left-wing Republicans and right-wing Nationalists
Economic instability and social reforms under the Second Spanish Republic
Military dissatisfaction with Republican reforms and civilian control
Failure of democratic institutions to resolve political conflicts
outcome: Nationalist victory and establishment of Francoist dictatorship
Spain remained neutral in WWII but aligned with Axis sympathies
Long-term political repression and exile of Republican supporters
Cultural and intellectual diaspora that influenced global politics

figures.name: Francisco Franco
figures.role: Nationalist leader and later dictator of Spain

impacts: Preceded and influenced WWII tactics and ideological conflicts
Created massive refugee crisis and cultural diaspora
Established authoritarian regime that lasted until 1975
Became symbol of anti-fascist resistance and ideological struggle
